compiled_state.title: [tests/scripts/test-dso-shim-subdir-dispatch.sh]: dispatched scripts hang under CI load -> TIMEOUT (exceeded 120s) instead of fast-fail
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Incident Overview

### Expected Behavior
The three test assertions in test-dso-shim-subdir-dispatch.sh invoke `$SHIM sprint-drift-check.sh BOGUS_EPIC_ID_xyz` etc. expecting fast-fail (exit code != 127, stderr not containing 'command not found'). Each invocation should complete in <5s.

### Actual Behavior
Observed during 2026-05-18 batch-fix session (PR #220 CI): `test-dso-shim-subdir-dispatch.sh ... TIMEOUT (exceeded 120s)`. The 120s suite ceiling fires, the test reports TIMEOUT (no actionable signal), and the entire CI run fails.

### Root Cause (likely)
Under CI load with /tmp contention, the shim's `find $DSO_ROOT/scripts -type f ...` (.claude/scripts/dso:138) is normally <1s but the downstream dispatched script (sprint-drift-check.sh, error-sweep.sh) performs real ticket-tracker queries that can hang on bogus IDs. The test's lack of bounded timeout converts the inner hang into a suite-level TIMEOUT.

### Suggested Fix
Wrap each SHIM call in `timeout 10s`:

```bash
stderr_out="$(timeout 10s "$SHIM" sprint-drift-check.sh BOGUS_EPIC_ID_xyz 2>&1 >/dev/null)" || exit_code=$?
```

`timeout` exits 124 on kill, distinct from 127 (command not found), so the existing `assert_ne \"127\"` check stays correct. A bounded timeout converts a TIMEOUT (unactionable) into either a deterministic PASS or a deterministic FAIL with an actionable failure mode.

### Companion Recommendation
File separate follow-up bugs on the dispatched scripts (sprint-drift-check.sh, error-sweep.sh) to add their own fast-fail behavior on bogus arguments. The test fix only stops the symptom from hiding.
